summary.headline: FY26 consolidated total income rose 46.93% to ₹221.72 crore, but standalone EBITDA fell 21.5% to ₹12.96 crore on margin investments.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of investment in capabilities, data centre, solar and semiconductor entry at tighter margins, and reported consolidated PAT of ₹15.82 crore (up 18.95%). Standalone PAT fell 24.75% to ₹9.06 crore, and standalone EBITDA fell 21.5% to ₹12.96 crore. Order book is stated at about ₹199 crore with a ₹480 crore pipeline, and management expects it to rise to ₹275–300 crore within about 15–20 days. Management flagged higher debt and working capital in FY27, with margin recovery and a larger takeoff expected from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: management says it has gone up since year end

segments.name: Kelvin Air Conditioning & Ventilation Systems (60.53% stake)
segments.commentary: HVAC arm providing complete system integration; management plans to raise stake to 70–72%. Expanding into data centres, industrial and solar.

segments.name: Advantek (34.99% stake after Altair merger)
segments.commentary: AHU manufacturer for backward integration. Altair merger caused a one-time ₹1 crore legacy hit; management expects EU certification to drive growth.

segments.name: Aart Integrated Projects (28% stake)
segments.commentary: Design and engineering arm for semiconductor, solar and non-pharma. Revenue reportedly rose from ₹14 crore to ₹34 crore, driven by non-pharma and microelectronics wins.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to 20–30% growth in FY27, described as conservative; it aims to hold margins while revenue grows.
Largest solar ticket (Waaree, ~₹68 crore) expected to be commissioned by July 2026.
Order book of ~₹199 crore expected to rise to ₹275–300 crore within 15–20 days; execution targeted by September–October 2026.
Management said the ~₹1 crore Altair drag and ~₹80 lakh NCLT-related write-off will not recur, implying about ₹18 crore PAT without them.
Management said H2 is historically stronger than H1 over the last four to five years.
capex_capacity: Hyderabad facility on about 2 acres, ~50,000 sq ft built-up area, capacity ~2,000 sq m per day, with one puff line and one rock wool panel line.
Factory capacity described as significantly enhanced and automated; gas and power shortages forced use of cylinders.
Management said no acquisitions are currently planned; focus is on consolidating existing entities.
demand_pricing: Solar: about 23 active hot leads; Waaree reference being completed; Satvik and Gupin references being established.
Semiconductor: CG Electronics AHU-based cleanroom cited as reference, under confidentiality; management said Japanese competitors are already present.
Data centres: project slowed as technology shifted from conventional HVAC to immersion cooling.
Pricing: company is seeking price revisions from clients under force majeure due to raw material (aluminium, steel) inflation and supply disruption.
Management accepted tighter margins on data centre, solar and semiconductor orders to build references.

qa_highlights.question: How will the order book diversify from solar into semiconductor, data centres and biotech?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said solar references were built first, with a pipeline of about 23 hot solar leads. Semiconductor entry will follow but faces Japanese incumbents, and life sciences turnkey remains the mainstay.

qa_highlights.question: Can the ₹200 crore order book be executed within H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was possible, with a caveat that client-requested start dates can push timelines; it expects the book to be executed within six months.

qa_highlights.question: Are large-ticket orders of ₹70–100 crore coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one or two orders of ₹60–80 crore were expected soon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the T-grid system and its TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Aart's Rajesh Gupte described a modular ceiling grid (1200x1200 mm) with FFU-based class control, load capacity of about 1,500–1,600 kg, and variants of 70, 130 and 210–230 mm heights; no TAM figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins on the current order book be normalised or lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin is subject to supply chain pressures; it is guiding to conservative growth and maintaining margins, with business decisions on new projects after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company acquire more capabilities or increase stakes in subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: No acquisition is currently planned. Stake increases in Kelvin (to 70–72%) and possibly Advantek are targeted, with Aart dependent on compliance readiness.

risks_watch: Working capital and debt rising in FY27 as retention money is pending; management expects improvement only from FY28.
Supply chain and raw material shortages (aluminium, steel, gas, power) with price revision requests to clients not guaranteed.
Standalone EBITDA and PAT declined sharply; consolidated gains rely on subsidiaries such as Aart and Kelvin.
Governance: information security issue addressed, NCLT-related write-off, and management acknowledged subsidiaries need better compliance.
Waaree commissioning slipping from schedule; delivery started in February 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term positioning and the order book, but evasive on specific margins, FY27 numbers and the Waaree delay. Management answered several questions with generalities and deferred others.
key_quotes: We are entering the new year with 199 and in 15 days time you will see the numbers going to upwards of 275 to 300 crores.
FY26 was a year of preparation and position. The foundation for the next phase of growth is now largely in place.
